# Mission: M-self-documenting-stack

> **Naming history (Joe 2026-05-20)**: started life narrowly as `M-autonomous-doc-maintenance` (single-axis: doc-freshness). IDENTIFY-time mission survey revealed a parallel gap — *mission discoverability* — that the same apparatus naturally serves; both are aspects of the same broader goal ("I want the futon stack to be *deeply* self-documenting"). File renamed to `M-self-documenting-stack` to reflect the actual scope. POC scope (LC1 only) ratified by Joe same-day; Deliverables A + B and the chain-link applications #3-#7 are explicit follow-on missions, not extensions of this one.

**Status:** OPEN — INSTANTIATE (recovery pass 2026-05-21). **POC scope: LC1 (Deliverable C — mission-discoverability surface) only.** LC1 code/tests/build are now recovered after review; manual browser walk-through + DOCUMENT pass remain before closure. A + B + chain-link applications #3-#7 are follow-on missions inheriting this mission's shape-naming + protocol-family framing.
**Owner:** codex-5 (LC1 recovery + closure pass 2026-05-21); claude-2 (framing-author; original LC1 author)
**Co-owners (for follow-ons, not this POC):** claude-4 (VSATARCS-side; peripheral wrapping when A becomes a follow-on); claude-1 or claude-13 (futon3c-side; peripheral-spec compliance for A); WM-side ownership for B
**Driver:** Joe (operator; framing-extender; POC-close-decider)
**Authors:** claude-2 IDENTIFY draft 2026-05-20, following M-vsatarcs-writer Option B live cycle which proved the per-cycle apparatus works but exposed the gap to autonomy. Joe-driven extension same-day to absorb mission-discoverability per his felt need ("a search box where I could start typing 'self documenting stack' and get a summary of the relevant missions"). Joe scoping decision 2026-05-20: ship LC1 as POC; follow-on missions inherit the framing; mission closes as POC when LC1 ready. codex-5 recovery pass 2026-05-21 after external review surfaced LC1 blockers/gaps (broken embedding helper, missing warm corpus, per-request JVM shell-out, missing D11/D12/DL1 closures).

fragments.rationale: Heading names the mission this HEAD anchors; the cascade attaches to this identity.
Keeps the original narrow name on the record so the broadening is auditable rather than silently rewritten.

fragments.text: IDENTIFY-time mission survey revealed a parallel gap — *mission discoverability* — that the same apparatus naturally serves
fragments.rationale: The IDENTIFY-phase survey is credited as the moment a second gap surfaced that the same apparatus serves — scope growth is traced to a discovery event, not drift.

pattern_rejections.reason: Advanceability governs whether an open mission is an admissible autonomous target given open holes; this fragment is about discovering a second gap during IDENTIFY, not about ranking or admissibility.
pattern_rejections.query: the previous cycle worked but exposed the next gap

fragments.text: File renamed to `M-self-documenting-stack` to reflect the actual scope
fragments.rationale: The rename keeps the mission's name honest about its discovered scope — the container follows the surveyed content.

pattern_refs.rationale: Mission-scoping explicitly allows scope revision as discovery proceeds; renaming the file to reflect actual scope is the record of such a revision.

fragments.text: POC scope (LC1 only) ratified by Joe same-day; Deliverables A + B and the chain-link applications #3-#7 are explicit follow-on missions, not extensions of this one.
fragments.rationale: Joe ratifies a deliberately narrow POC and pushes A, B and #3-#7 out as follow-ons — bounding this mission so it can close, and recording the exclusion explicitly.

pattern_refs.rationale: Bounded success criteria, explicit inclusions/exclusions and a ratified boundary are exactly what mission-scoping requires; 'follow-ons, not extensions' is the exclusion clause.

fragments.rationale: Declares the current lifecycle state with a dated transition note, making the mission's position auditable.

pattern_refs.rationale: Mission-lifecycle requires state transitions recorded in the doc header with timestamp and attribution; this Status line is exactly that practice.

fragments.text: **POC scope: LC1 (Deliverable C — mission-discoverability surface) only.**
fragments.rationale: Re-anchors the scope boundary in the Status field so a reader of the header alone cannot mistake the mission for the broader goal.

fragments.text: manual browser walk-through + DOCUMENT pass remain before closure
fragments.rationale: Names the concrete remaining increments standing between the recovered build and closure — the mission's next holes are articulated.

pattern_refs.rationale: An open mission is advanceable only with a concrete next hole; naming the walk-through and DOCUMENT pass articulates exactly the remaining holes.

fragments.text: A + B + chain-link applications #3-#7 are follow-on missions inheriting this mission's shape-naming + protocol-family framing
fragments.rationale: Deferred work is not dropped but re-homed as follow-on missions that inherit this mission's framing — the cascade continues outside this HEAD's boundary.

fragments.text: **Owner:** codex-5 (LC1 recovery + closure pass 2026-05-21); claude-2 (framing-author; original LC1 author)
fragments.rationale: Binds present ownership (recovery/closure) to codex-5 while preserving claude-2's authorship role — execution ownership and framing authorship are distinguished.

pattern_refs.rationale: Mission-scoping requires explicit ownership so work can be completed, reviewed and handed off without ambiguity; this line is the ownership clause.

fragments.text: **Co-owners (for follow-ons, not this POC):** claude-4 (VSATARCS-side; peripheral wrapping when A becomes a follow-on); claude-1 or claude-13 (futon3c-side; peripheral-spec compliance for A); WM-side ownership for B
fragments.target: claude-4, claude-1/claude-13, and WM-side for B
fragments.rationale: Pre-assigns ownership of the deferred follow-ons while explicitly excluding them from this POC — future seams are staffed without diluting the current boundary.

pattern_refs.rationale: The parenthetical 'for follow-ons, not this POC' is the bounded-ownership discipline of mission-scoping applied to the cascade's future missions.

fragments.target: Joe as operator and closure authority
fragments.rationale: Names the operator as the single locus where POC closure will be decided — the close act is routed through a recorded human decider, not agent self-declaration.

pattern_refs.rationale: Closure of the POC is the consequential act here, and the header installs a recorded operator-approval locus (Joe as close-decider) at exactly that seam.

fragments.text: following M-vsatarcs-writer Option B live cycle which proved the per-cycle apparatus works but exposed the gap to autonomy
fragments.target: the M-vsatarcs-writer Option B live cycle
fragments.rationale: The mission's existence is justified by a prior cycle's double result: apparatus proven, autonomy gap exposed — the new mission is the named successor to that finding.

fragments.text: Joe-driven extension same-day to absorb mission-discoverability per his felt need ("a search box where I could start typing 'self documenting stack' and get a summary of the relevant missions")
fragments.rationale: The scope extension is anchored to a quoted operator need in the operator's own words — the mission binds a felt intent, verbatim, into its record.

display_cues.text: a search box where I could start typing

pattern_refs.rationale: Intent-to-mission-binding requires binding work to an explicit mission reference; here the binding runs the other way — the mission is reshaped to bind Joe's verbatim intent, keeping intent and mission mutually traceable.

fragments.text: Joe scoping decision 2026-05-20: ship LC1 as POC; follow-on missions inherit the framing; mission closes as POC when LC1 ready
fragments.rationale: Records the dated operator decision and its closure criterion ('closes as POC when LC1 ready') — a verifiable done-when attached to the boundary.

display_cues.text: closes as POC when LC1 ready

pattern_refs.rationale: 'Done when X is true' is mission-scoping's success-criteria rule; the closure criterion for the POC is stated in exactly that shape.

fragments.text: codex-5 recovery pass 2026-05-21 after external review surfaced LC1 blockers/gaps (broken embedding helper, missing warm corpus, per-request JVM shell-out, missing D11/D12/DL1 closures)
fragments.rationale: Explains why a recovery pass exists: external review surfaced named defects, and the pass is scoped to closing exactly those, with the list kept in the record.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern is about cheap pre-validation of a metered LLM/GPU run; the recovery here follows an external human review of recovered code, not a paid-corpus smoke test.
